note.text: In this course, African nationalism means movements and ideas asserting a people’s right to determine its political future, especially to end colonial domination. A campaign could begin with demands for rights or representation and later seek independence; the stages were not identical everywhere. A nation is not simply one ethnic group, and nationalist movements could unite people across language or regional differences. Pan-Africanism promoted solidarity among Africans and people of African descent across territorial boundaries. Nationalism and Pan-Africanism could reinforce one another without being interchangeable.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish demands for collective self-government from a limited reform and explain how nationalism differed from Pan-Africanism. Builds on: colonial rule, wartime change and the limits of Brazzaville. Leads to: the internal and external factors strengthening nationalist movements.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: In this course, African nationalism means movements and ideas asserting a people’s right to determine its political future, especially to end colonial domination. A campaign could begin with demands for rights or representation and later seek independence; the stages were not identical everywhere. A nation is not simply one ethnic group, and nationalist movements could unite people across language or regional differences. Pan-Africanism promoted solidarity among Africans and people of African descent across territorial boundaries. Nationalism and Pan-Africanism could reinforce one another without being interchangeable.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: A petition for fair pay addresses an immediate grievance. A demand that inhabitants control the territory’s government raises the wider issue of self-government. A Pan-African meeting connects struggles across territories and the diaspora. Methods included petitions, associations, newspapers, unions, elections and, in some settings, armed struggle. No method alone defines every nationalist movement. Leaders disagreed over aims and tactics, and claims to represent a nation must be examined alongside the experiences of workers, women, rural communities and minorities.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the political objective rather than labelling every protest nationalist automatically. Ask who should govern, whose rights are claimed and how broadly support is organised. Distinguish solidarity across Africa from one territory’s constitutional objective. Explain a movement’s programme without treating all its assertions as established facts or assuming that national unity eliminated internal disagreement.

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.
example: An association demands that inhabitants determine the territory’s future government.
People from several language groups campaign together for control of their territory’s government.
Delegates from different territories coordinate opposition to colonial domination.
A workers’ petition asks for a pay rise without stating a constitutional objective.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Self-determination means permanent rule without the inhabitants’ wishes. Correction: The concept concerns political choice by the people, not their exclusion from deciding.
A nationalist coalition must consist of only one ethnic group. Correction: A territorial movement can organise across ethnic and regional differences.
Pan-Africanism concerns only one village’s private arrangements. Correction: Its scope crosses territorial boundaries, even when participants also pursue local national goals.
Every request for improved pay explicitly demands independence. Correction: A wage demand may connect to nationalism but does not by itself specify independent statehood.
